title: CNL fourth-anniversary ceremony planned for Bujumbura on 19 February was suspended
reason: The contemporaneous report says the Minister of Interior suspended the planned double ceremony and a ministry source told SOS Médias it would not take place. The scheduled event is not an observed gathering.
notes: The report also describes internal CNL meetings on 17–18 February, but gives no attendance or public protest action. A later March report describes a CNL congress and celebration of the same fourth anniversary on 12 March; possible rescheduling is unresolved and this excluded February plan is not merged or backdated.
open_questions: Whether the March 12 celebration was a rescheduling of the suspended February ceremony is not expressly stated; keep the actual March event separate unless stronger evidence resolves linkage.

title: Bujumbura police sweep of unemployed youths and policy complaints in administrative-measures dossier
reason: The report describes youths individually arrested and transported to a construction site, and interviews vendors and butchers about official rules and prices. It does not describe a public assembly making a government demand; the individual complaints and police action are not an executed protest gathering.
notes: The article mentions that some youths had been congregating around kiosks, but the reporting describes police detentions rather than an organized collective protest. Approximately twenty people transported in the police vehicle are not a turnout count for an anti-state gathering.

title: Province-wide support marches for President Ndayishimiye
reason: ABP reports a march of support and congratulations for the sitting President after his AU role. This is pro-government political support, not a demand against the domestic state; event date falls in February despite March publication.
notes: ABP describes events in different provinces; no attendance is pooled across sites. This lead is retained for onset-month ownership and excluded under the anti-state protest definition.
